numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Rolling covariance/correlation values are silently wrong after a large value leaves the sliding window; can also become NaN once a negative ssqdm_x is used in the square root in calc_corr.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Rolling cov/corr should not be poisoned by earlier numerical error; instead it should recompute or otherwise re-anchor/bound incremental accumulators so results match exact values for windows, and avoid NaN/poisoning once a negative ssqdm_x would be involved in calc_corr. The passage’s example exact expected values are [1.1, -0.3, -0.8].
trigger_conditions: Rolling cov/corr over a window after the series contains a large shared offset (example uses adding 1e12 to both x and y)
After a window that previously included a very large value leaves the window, every later window is silently wrong
Numerical instability in which ssqdm_x collapses such that it becomes negative and calc_corr takes a square root of a negative number, producing NaN

Execution paths where the incremental cov/corr logic only checked catastrophic cancellation for ssqdm_xy against its own previous value and missed that ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y collapse to round-off after the dominating value leaves the window
Incremental recomputation logic that does not bound error using the largest deviation each accumulator has absorbed since the last recompute

input_output_examples.input: x = pd.Series([1, 2, 4, 7, 3, 5, 9, 2, 6, 8], dtype="float64") + 1e12; y = pd.Series([2, 1, 5, 3, 8, 4, 7, 9, 1, 6], dtype="float64") + 1e12; x.rolling(5).cov(y).iloc[4:7].tolist()

oracle_clues: Commit text: "Every window after a large value left was silently wrong, or NaN once a negative ssqdm_x reached the square root in calc_corr."
PR#66678 reproducer shows exact expected values: "exact: [1.1, -0.3, -0.8]" for x.rolling(5).cov(y).iloc[4:7].tolist(), whereas produced values were "[1.099968..., -0.300072..., -0.800026...]".

Commit fix description: incremental cov/corr accumulators missed two issues—(1) ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y collapse to round-off after the dominating value leaves the window and (2) error from an earlier update is invisible one step later.

Commit fix description: bound error by using the largest deviation each accumulator absorbed since the last recompute (test all three accumulators against it). Also anchor accumulators to the first value in the window so a common offset cancels exactly; values large enough that subtraction could overflow are not used as an anchor.

C code excerpt indicates new logic tracks peak deviations (track_peak_dev) and uses cancellation_suspected(ssqdm_xy[0], ssqdm_x[0], ssqdm_y[0], peak_dev_x[0], peak_dev_y[0]) to decide numerically_unstable/recompute.

commit message: rolling cov/corr wrong after a large value leaves the window; incremental accumulators: ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y collapse to round-off as soon as dominating value leaves the window; error introduced by earlier update is invisible one step later; 'Every window after a large value left was silently wrong, or NaN once a negative ssqdm_x reached the square root in calc_corr.'

commit message: separately, deviations were taken against a mean that is itself huge when the series carries a large shared offset, leaving almost no significant digits; fix: anchor accumulators to the first value in the window so a common offset cancels exactly; 'values large enough that the subtraction could overflow are not used as an anchor'

aggregations.pyx: InvCondTol is EpsF64*1e3 and addition of MaxOriginMagnitude=np.sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).max) with comment that subtracting an origin of this size can never overflow and beyond it squared deviations would overflow anyway (relevant to magnitude regimes where anchoring is/ isn't safe)
reproduction_risks: Bug depends on dtype float64 (code uses float64_t and the reproducer specifies dtype='float64'); reproducer must keep float64 inputs.

Bug appears in magnitude regimes involving large values/shared offsets (on order 1e12 and also includes 1e12/-1e12 in the test); smaller magnitudes may not trigger the cancellation/accumulator collapse behavior.

The failure mode includes NaN poisoning for later windows when ssqdm_x becomes negative and calc_corr takes sqrt of a negative number; reproducer should include subsequent windows after a large value leaves (e.g., rolling after the outlier exits).
Correctness separation is described via rtol=1e-12 and atol=0 for expected incremental update tolerance; using different tolerances may mask or exaggerate the discrepancy.
